title: Customs Tariff Amendment (Japan-Australia Economic Partnership Agreement Implementation) Bill 2014
short_title: Customs Tariff Amendment (Japan-Australia Economic Partnership Agreement Implementation) Bill 2014

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: This bill changes the Customs Tariff Act 1995 to put into effect the Japan-Australia Economic Partnership Agreement.

It sets zero customs duty on goods that qualify as Japanese originating goods under a new part of the Customs Act 1901, adjusts some existing tariff rates, and phases other preferential rates to zero by 2021.
The bill also adds a new schedule to the tariff to hold the preferential, phasing, and excise-equivalent rates on certain alcohol, tobacco, and petroleum products.
changes: Provides free rates of customs duty for Japanese originating goods.
Amends Schedule 4 to keep certain duty rates for Japanese goods.
Phases preferential rates for some goods to Free by 2021.
Inserts a new Schedule 11 for preferential, phasing, and excise-equivalent rates.
summary.affected: Importers of Japanese goods and the Australian Customs Tariff system.

speeches.speaker: Andrew Robb
speeches.brief: Moved the second reading of the Customs Amendment (Japan-Australia Economic Partnership Agreement Implementation) Bill 2014, said more than 97 per cent of Australia's exports to Japan would receive preferential access or enter duty-free once fully implemented, and noted the agreement was signed on 8 July 2014 by Prime Minister Tony Abbott and Japanese Prime Minister Shinzo Abe.

speeches.speaker: Andrew Robb
speeches.brief: Moved the second reading of the Customs Tariff Amendment (Japan-Australia Economic Partnership Agreement Implementation) Bill 2014, which phases preferential tariff rates on Japanese-originating goods to zero by 2021, and creates a new schedule setting excise-equivalent duties on certain alcohol, tobacco and petroleum products.

speeches.speaker: Tanya Plibersek
speeches.brief: Argued that Labor supports the Japan-Australia Economic Partnership Agreement bills but moved a second reading amendment opposing investor-state dispute settlement provisions, criticised the exemption from labour market testing for 457 visa contractual service providers from Japan, and cited industry criticism from groups such as the National Farmers Federation.

speeches.speaker: Russell Matheson
speeches.brief: Moved the Customs Tariff Amendment (Japan-Australia Economic Partnership Agreement Implementation) Bill 2014, arguing that the agreement would give more than 97 per cent of Australia's trade with Japan preferential or duty-free access, benefit beef and dairy exporters, and support farmers, businesses and consumers.

speeches.speaker: David Gillespie
speeches.brief: Supported the two bills implementing the Japan-Australia Economic Partnership Agreement, arguing that lower tariffs would improve export competitiveness, farm-gate prices and regional employment, and citing opportunities for beef, dairy, wine, timber and macadamia producers.

speeches.speaker: Andrew Robb
speeches.brief: Concluded debate on the Customs Tariff Amendment (Japan-Australia Economic Partnership Agreement Implementation) Bill 2014, explaining that it implements Australia's tariff commitments under the Japan-Australia agreement; reported its effects on agriculture, resources and services, including a tariff-free quota of 20,000 tonnes for cheese and a 10 per cent initial reduction for frozen beef.
